title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 2 of the notational preliminaries for the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power De Rham complex. It sets up four things.

(1) Notation for simplicial objects. For a category A, an object of A_* = Hom(Δ°, A) is written K_* = (K_[n])_{n≥0}, better as Δ^n ↦ K_[n], together with its face and degeneracy maps. Grothendieck insists on writing K_[n] rather than K_n. The reason is announced but not given here: when A is additive, the plain subscript will presumably be kept for the associated (normalized or Moore) chain complex under Dold–Kan. Dually, an object of A^* = Hom(Δ, A) is written K^* = (n ↦ K^[n]).

(2) Transport of variance by a duality. Suppose v: A° ≃ B is an equivalence, M ↦ M^v. Typically A = B and v is an involution with the usual compatibility (M^vv ≅ M). Then v sends a simplicial object of A to a cosimplicial object of B and conversely: K^* = (K_*)^v, K^[n] = (K_[n])^v. The same letter is used for both, and only the position of the star records the variance. The main example: k is a ring, A is finitely generated projective left k-modules, B is the same on the right, and v = Hom_k(-, k). If k is commutative this is an autoduality of A.

(3) The Yoneda embedding Δ ↪ Ŝs is fully faithful. The image of Δ^n is written Δ^n_*, better Δ^[n]_* since it is covariant in n. It is the representable simplicial set m ↦ Hom_Δ(Δ^m, Δ^n), and Hom(Δ^n_*, X_*) ≅ X_[n]. In particular Hom(Δ^n_*, Δ^m_*) ≅ Hom_ord(Δ^n, Δ^m). Since n ↦ Δ^n_* is covariant, the embedding is itself a cosimplicial simplicial set. Grothendieck names it the 'universal cosimplicial object' and writes it Δ^*_* ∈ (Ss)^*.

(4) Two-index notation. An object of (A_*)^* ≅ Hom(Δ × Δ°, A) is written K^*_*, with components K^[m]_[n]. The next page extends this to K_*^*, K^**, K_** and to symmetry operators.

Purpose: a uniform 'universal algebra' notation for simplicial and cosimplicial modules and their linear duals. This is clearly preparing a duality between simplicial and cosimplicial constructions over projective k-modules. Such a duality is the natural way to bring in divided powers, using Γ^n(M) ≅ (Sym^n(M^v))^v, and to compare Dold–Puppe-type functors on simplicial modules with their cosimplicial duals, as needed for a divided-power De Rham complex.
errors: Writing Δ^m_*(Δ^n_*) for Δ^m_*(Δ^n) is a harmless abuse of notation, not a mathematical error.

The page itself has no substantive errors. (On the neighbouring page the transcription gives (A^*)^* ≃ Hom(Δ°×Δ, A); it should be Hom(Δ×Δ, A). That is a slip on the next page, or in its transcription, not here.)

ideas.what: Notation K_[n] for the components of a simplicial object, keeping the plain subscript for the associated complex in the additive case
A duality A° ≃ B (dual of f.g. projective modules) exchanges simplicial and cosimplicial objects
ideas.modern_name: Linear duality between simplicial and cosimplicial modules

ideas.what: Yoneda embedding Δ → Ŝs viewed as the universal cosimplicial simplicial set Δ^*_*
ideas.modern_name: Cosimplicial object of standard simplices / Yoneda embedding (the basis of Kan extensions and realization-nerve adjunctions)
ideas.where_published: Similar viewpoint appears in Pursuing Stacks (1983), but not in this exact form

ideas.what: Index-position convention for bisimplicial, bicosimplicial and mixed objects (K^*_*, etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely notational groundwork: simplicial/cosimplicial notation, duality transport and the Yoneda embedding as a universal cosimplicial object. Everything is standard. Its only interest is as context for the planned divided-power construction.
transcription_corrections: The parenthesis after 'pour des raisons qui vont apparaître' seems to read '(simpli-[fications?] lorsque A est additive ...)', not 'simplicielles'.
'notée M ↦ M^v' in the image is closer to '(notée M ↦ M̌)', i.e. with a check accent.
In 'A = k-modules à g. proj. de t.f.', 'à g.' means 'à gauche' (left modules).
